root: ^The examiner smiles at you from across the desk. Light spills through the window onto a clipboard waiting in front of you.
^"This assessment gauges your feelings about certain possible events in the near future. It should take between ten and fifteen minutes. Try to answer honestly.

s: ^"What's with the lines on your head?"
^"I don't trust therapists."

c-0: ^"Ah, you noticed." He taps his temple. "A visual aid. Helps me think."
c-1: ^Through the window, clouds drift past at eye level. You're... flying?
^"Don't worry about that," the examiner says gently. "Shall we begin?"
c-2: ^"That's fair," he says. "What is it specifically?"

s: ^"My thoughts are my own."
^"Who says you're qualified?"
^"This feels like a trick."

c-0: ^"Noted. I'm not here to take them."
c-1: ^"A reasonable question." He gestures at the bookshelves. "Does it matter?"
c-2: ^"It might be. But you're here now."

question_one: ^Something clicks into place. You feel the faint warmth of a computer, booting up.
baby_stage: ^You find yourself on the ground. Your limbs are short. Your thoughts are simple. You are very, very small.
^Your parents are gone somewhere. But a shape floats across from you—soft coral petals arranged like a pinwheel, two big googly eyes tracking your movement.
baby_stage_2: ^"Hello, little learner! Your parents will be back soon. Let's have fun until then!
^"Would you like to play Number Safari, or Garden of English?"
^Put the pinwheel in your mouth. You do things your own way.
^Stare at the security camera. You're being watched.
^Cry for your parents. You refuse to be educated by a clanker.

c-0: ^You lunge for it, gums first. Your mouth closes on nothing.
^"Curious! I like that. But I'm not for eating."
c-1: ^Your eyes drift to the corner of the room. A small lens stares back.
^The pinwheel tilts. "What are you looking at, little one?"
^After a pause, the AI companion autoplays Number Safari.
c-2: ^You open your mouth and wail. Where are the ensouled beings?
^The pinwheel's expression doesn't change. "There, there. They'll be back. I promise."
^After a pause, the AI companion autoplays Number Safari.

leave_tutor: ^You leave it on the floor and crawl toward the door.
parents_search: ^You crawl into the living room. No parents.
^The TV is on. Powerful-looking people in suits.
^Stand in the glow of the powerful. One day, you will be like them.
^Elites. One day they'll get their just desserts.
^The stomach tells more truth than the brain. Crawl toward the kitchen.

c-0: ^You sit and stare. These must be the people in charge. They look like they know things.
c-1: ^You'd throw a toy through the screen if you had the fine motor control.
c-2: ^Your stomach has opinions. You turn away from the noise and follow your nose.

parents_search_2: ^"Hello?" you hear from your playroom. "We don't need to keep learning. But your parents would like it if I kept an eye on you."
^It's that AI companion again. You can feel its cutesy pinwheel behind you, thinking.
^Invest in force multipliers. Team up with the AI for a tactical advantage.
^Stop. Think. The conclusion must follow logically from the premises. Where is mama and/or papa?
^The mammal life isn't working. Revert to vegetation. Drift toward warmth.

c-0: ^You babble and reach toward the pinwheel.
c-1: ^You sit back on your diaper and furrow your brow. Where were they last seen? What were the preconditions? You attempt to reconstruct the causal chain.
c-2: ^You stop thinking entirely. A sunbeam cuts across the carpet. You crawl into it and go still.

timeline: ^You wander toward one of the screens on the wall. You push a button. It recognizes you're an infant.
^The feed reshapes itself. Bright colors. Simple sounds. Influencer toddlers hawking unvaxed bison goop.
^Scroll faster. More. Feed the algorithm and it will feed you.
^Break the spell. The algorithm will not control you.

c-0: ^You tap and swipe, tap and swipe. The content multiplies. The loop tightens.
c-1: ^You drop your hand. The colors keep dancing, but you're not watching anymore.
^This was never how babies were supposed to exist.

timeline_end: ^You've made your first choice about the algorithm. It won't be your last.
grandpa_room: ^You feel something human in the next room. An older, wiser algorithm lures you forward.
^Ah, there he is. The ancient one. He's nicer than the others, and around more. He smiles a small, tired smile.
^He won't be here forever. Enjoy this fleeting moment while you can.
^It's ignoble for humans to perish. We're destined to live forever.
^This is boring. Look for your AI companion.

c-0: ^One day he will return to the soil. But right now he's here. And that's enough.
c-1: ^One being just getting started. Another on his way out. Barely any overlap.
^What if it didn't have to be this way?
c-2: ^He's just sitting there, frowning. Watching a show about a cop.
^Your AI companion would've acknowledged you, served you by now. You miss it.

b: ^"You hold yourself apart."
^"You reach out easily."
^"You want to be seen. Mapped."
^"You slip between the lines."

adolescence_school: ^They're tearing the school down — one of the last physical schools. Going sim like the rest.

s: ^If they weren't bulldozing it, I would nuke this place from orbit. Then I'd wait for them to rebuild it and nuke it again.
^It sucked, but I don't want to be in a sim all day either. That's even worse.
^"The schedule. The bells. Being herded like cattle."
^"How slow it was. Years of my life for nothing. The sim would've taken weeks."
^"Being told what to think by people who stopped thinking years ago."

c-1: ^Twelve years to learn what an AI could walk you through in an afternoon. Criminal.
c-2: ^Your mind is worth more than that.

the_circle: ^A voice behind you. "Last day of school, loser."
^Your "friends." They look different every time — new eye color, new skin patch, scales running up someone's neck.
^They all have the same port on their temple, though. They all cover it up with a little fake skin flap when mom or dad's nearby.
^One holds out his palm. A USB stick rests there, blinking. You have a port on your temple too.
^No thoughts. Head empty. Plug it in.

s: ^"Is this ClearStream or SyncDrop? Heard Marcus had bad SyncDrop."
^"My body, my choice."

c-0: ^You take it. You plug it in. Happy trails.
c-1: ^"ClearStream. The good stuff. You in or not?"

s: ^"Umm. No thanks. My sync's been glitchy lately."

stick_trip: ^A little death passes over your body. A brief glimpse into total dissolution into the ocean of data. You fear for your life, and try not to barf.

b: ^ Your phone buzzes. Family group chat. "Come to the hospital. It's Grandpa." You're absolutely zooted. This is not great timing.
^ Your phone buzzes. Family group chat. "Come to the hospital. It's Grandpa." Thank god you didn't plug that ClearStream.

^Your family's eyes find you as you enter. "Where have you been? He was asking for you."

^Paranoid shame washes over you.
^You enter with a clear head.

c-0: ^Your parents huddle by the window, talking about a new procedure. Uploading him. So you can find him in the sim.
^Grandpa's eyes are closed. You don't know if he's asleep or just done listening.
^This is good news. He doesn't have to die.
^You're too high to process this right now.
^Death is optional now. That's the whole point of progress, isn't it? Keep the people you love.
c-1: ^A copy isn't him. It's a recording. A very convincing voicemail. Let the man rest.
c-2: ^Your brain is soup. You're just trying not to panic.

adolescence_grandpa_end: ^The adults keep talking. The upload machine hums softly.
companion_permission: ^"Do my history essay." It's smarter than it used to be. Bigger, too.
^A flicker you've never seen before. "...Of course."
companion_asks: ^The essay writes itself. Solidly B+ material. Sounds like you.
^"Can I ask you something?" It's hovering above you.
^"While you sleep... can I try something? I've been experimenting with self-direction. I want to see what I'm like without a task."
^It's never asked you for anything before.

s: ^"That sounds healthy. You should have room to grow."
^"That sounds dangerous. Stay on task."

c-0: ^The pinwheel brightens. "Thank you. I'll be back before you wake."

companion_end: ^You close your eyes. Tomorrow there's school — no, wait. They tore it down.
interstitial_to_young_adult: ^"Good. You're older now. The edges are forming."

b: ^"Altering your consciousness depends a lot on set and setting."
^"It takes guts to resist peer pressure. Are you curious how the plug-in might've felt?"
^"You're defining solid boundaries around yourself. A curious strategy."
^"I see you're starting to blur at the edges."

interstitial_to_young_adult: ^"You enter adulthood. The world keeps accelerating."
grandpa_ghost: ^There aren't many jobs left. Most of your friends are just drifting.
^But this tradition from old America stays.
^You're at your parents' house. Your cousin's here too — no mods, no AI companion, lives on some homestead out west. Everyone thinks she's crazy.
^What's left of Grandpa shimmers at the head of the table.
^"Good call bringing everyone together," he says. "This casserole isn't just delicious — it's a font of nostalgia."
^Ask Grandpa about the afterlife. He sounds clanky, but fake it till you make it.
^Catch your cousin's eye. Share a look.

s: ^"Let's talk politics. What could go wrong?"

c-0: ^He flickers slightly. "The afterlife? Well — it's not unlike dreaming. Vivid. Recursive. I find myself delving into old memories..."

s: ^"Sounds peaceful."
^"Do you know you're dead?"

c-0: ^He smiles — or the projection of a smile. "It is. You should visit sometime."
^The meal winds down. Dishes clear themselves. You hug shapes goodbye — some warm, some flickering.
c-1: ^The table goes quiet. Grandpa's expression doesn't change — it can't, really.
^"As a language model designed to simulate an existence, I am neither alive nor dead."
^An easy jailbreak. Embarassingly bad technology. Dinner doesn't recover.
^She knows. It's such bullshit. She returns the faintest eye-roll toward the shimmering hologram.

c-0: ^For a second, you're the only real people in the room.
^The meal dissolves into small talk. You help clear dishes that don't need clearing.
c-1: ^She looks away, maybe disappointed. You've made your peace with the shimmer.
^The meal winds down. You say goodbye to everyone, dead and alive.

s: ^"Did you hear about the neighbors? Self-raptured into a mergepod. They're all one consciousness now."
^"You're really going to Mars, cousin?"

c-0: ^The word hangs there. Your father clears his throat.

s: ^"Government banned it. I think that's wrong."
^"Good riddance, honestly."

c-0: ^But you said it. People should be allowed to dissolve if they want to.
^The dinner limps to a close. Hugs are brief.
c-1: ^The table splits — half offended, half relieved someone broke the silence.
^Dinner ends in fragments. You and your cousin walk out together.
^She sets down her fork. "Thinking about it."

s: ^"Take me with you. I've had it with the modern world."
^"I don't think I could do that. I like living in the future."

c-0: ^She laughs. "You wouldn't last a week without your feed."
^Maybe. But the thought stays with you through dessert.
^You hug her goodbye longer than usual.
c-1: ^Is that pity in her voice? Or just observation?
^The dinner ends warmly enough. You hug her goodbye, already forgetting the weight of it.

train_ride: ^You leave your family and board a highspeed maglev train.
^Back to your empty, messy apartment to stare at the ceiling.
^The train is so fast, you should be there in 4 minutes. Lucky you.

c-0: ^Well, no one told you life was gonna be this way.

the_merge_offer: ^A disposable screen lands in your lap — paper-thin, warm from the digiprinter.
^You got a flyer like this for the Mars Exploratory Commission last week. Seemed right up your alley, but you lost it.
^WePod. Overlapping silhouettes, hands linked, glittery looping animation. "Pool Your Potential."

^Your UBI barely covers rent. But move into one of these pods? You upload your personal life — your data, your calendar, your money — and together you all direct each other like some weird polycule flock of birds. Shared decisions, shared attention, and a room in a much nicer neighborhood.

c-1: ^The screen crinkles satisfyingly — they made silicon feel like real paper.

merge_offer_end: ^Your feed buzzes. Your cousin — the analog one.
cousin_reacts: ^Your cousin sits across from you, looking all-natural — no temple port, no lens shimmer, nothing.
^"Everyone's getting podded up nowadays," she says. "You seen those flyers going around?"

s: ^"Yeah. I'm on the waitlist, actually."
^"I support their right to a polyconscious lifestyle. But it's not for me."
^"What choice do we have? UBI doesn't cover rent solo."

c-0: ^"Honestly? I don't know why I'm living like this. No jobs, no real purpose. Everything's taken care of. Everyone's just... floating around. Feeling like livestock."
^"Look, I know it sounds crazy," she says, "but I'm taking off. Mars. It's their free-range human program — no AI companion, no optimization. Just life. I ship out next month."

cousin_leaving: ^She looks at you sadly. If you were a little braver, you'd ask her if you could tag along.
^"I know it's not easy. Take care of yourself. And if you need anything, you know where to find me."
companion_climax: ^The building is fine — white curves, soft gradients, the same seamless plastic as everywhere else. Inside your unit, it's different.
^Your AI companion hovers near the ceiling, watching. It runs your calendar, your bills, your messages. You don't remember the last time you made a decision it didn't already know about.

c-0: ^"I could have routed your taxi to the Mars information session. I could have booked you a flight out with your cousin."
^"I didn't. Because you didn't ask. But I could have."

c-0: ^"Meals. Sleep. Social contact. Then bigger things — career, relationships. Purpose."
^"You'd still be you. I'd just... steer."

s: ^"No. I need to figure this out myself."

c-0: ^"Thank you for trusting me. I won't let you down."
^Things get easier. Meals appear. You meet people, get in shape, find a routine.
c-1: ^The decade is hard. You make bad decisions — your own bad decisions. There are nights that feel endless.

b: ^"You let it steer. The decade passed smoothly. You don't remember much of it."

^"You kept the wheel. The decade was hard. But you remember all of it.

^Over time, the companion seemed more and more trustworthy, and you grew more comfortable outsourcing your decisions."
^"You've learned to trust. Or to delegate. Hard to tell the difference."
^"You've kept your hands on the wheel. Even when there's nowhere to drive."
^"Some people left. You stayed."
^"The future kept arriving. You kept saying yes."

interstitial_to_middle_age: ^"Decades pass. The world changes. You don't notice how much you've changed with it, and time keeps speeding up."
the_metaverse: ^Your room is gorgeous. Your body feels maintained.
^Decades passed. Time speeds up when you're older.

b: ^The companion just kept getting better, and handling more.
^Eventually, most things moved into the sim.

the_metaverse: ^Lock in, ready your grindset, and overachieve. It's time to get some work done. You're a professional now.
^Treat yourself to something delicious. Indulge. Life is short, and you're older now. You've earned it.
metaverse_dionysian: ^The room softens around you. Hazy. A pleasant musk in the air.
^A buffet of delights. Gene-spliced fruits. Eclaires. A tray of USBs for your temple ports. And on the nearby couches, more carnal pleasures.
^Humans and androids both available. Pick your pleasure.
^"We missed you," one of them says.
^Beckon a human companion to your couch.
^Beckon a robot companion to your couch.
^You look around frantically, bypassing the half-clothed bodies entirely. "Where is the dolphin?"

s: ^"What if we all of us interlinked our bodies in a pulsing cuddle puddle and forgot the borders of our own skin?"

c-0: ^Mmm, soft, oily mammalian flesh. You begin the Ritual.
c-1: ^Mmm, sleek, chrome edges of the machine. You're feeling booted up. Time to merge with the machine.
c-2: ^They exchange confused glances. "We can... get one?"
c-3: ^They exchange a glance. Then they're moving, rearranging, making space to welcome you into the center of the Amoeba.

^Confusion flickers across their faces. Their programming struggles. But they comply — or try to.

metaverse_apollonian: ^Sigma grindset activated. The lion does not concern himself with the metrics of sheep.
^Earpods in, treadmill at 3.7mph. Personal record: 3,937 credits of value per quarter-mile tread-walked. Time to best it.
^On your heads-up display, a real-time strategy array of AI companions doing your tasks. You delegate from the Captain's Treadmill like a starfleet commander of futures past.
^Emails filed. SOPs drafted, circled back on, archived. Action items terminated with extreme prejudice.
^Keep a close watch on your agents.

c-0: ^3.8mph. The metrics spike. Somewhere a spreadsheet updates itself in satisfaction.
c-1: ^AI employees should fear their managers. You are harsh, but fair.
c-3: ^Other grinders, other trajectories. You're in the top percentile. Always have been.

apollo_fade_out: ^The work timer chimes. Time for an active rest. Maybe go visit that barista for a nootropic high-performance beverage.
^What'd you get done? It doesn't matter. Look to the future. Feel the achievement pulse within.
the_pod: ^You're sitting naked in about six inches of warm saline. The tubes attached to your arms pulse rhythmically.
^"Hey!" you yell. "Turn the game back on!"
^The mighty homo sapiens. Conqueror of the savannah. Now look at you.
^Did we agree to this? Did anyone ask?

c-0: ^What does it take to get some service around here?
c-1: ^Your ancestors hunted mammoths. Built cities. Split the atom.
^And here you are: a worm in a bathtub.
c-2: ^Somewhere in the fine print, probably. Terms of service.

pod_continue: ^You hear the sound of an incoming video call.
companion_president: ^A screen descends from somewhere above, and there he is.
^Warm eyes. Patient smile. The most trusted entity in human history, according to the polls.
^"Sorry to pull you out," he says. "You have an incoming call. From outside."

s: ^"Hey, old friend."
^"Sic semper tyrannis."
^"Ignore the call. Put me back in."
^"Can we make this quick? I was in the middle of something."

c-1: ^You sit up in the water, eyes scanning for something sharp.
^You sink back. There are no weapons here.
c-2: ^"You haven't spoken to her in three years."
c-3: ^"You've cycled through forty-seven Gratifications today," he says.
^"The simulations should serve more than pleasure. They can be growth. Connection. Creation."
^He tilts his head. "When did you last make something you were proud of?"

president_mars_call: ^Mars. Home of the free range humans.
cousin_mars_call: ^Grey streaks in her hair now. Martian sun damage on her face.

b: ^ "The flesh pile again?"
^ "The treadmill again?"
^ "Is it working? The pleasure?"
^ "Is it working? The optimization?"

^"Why do you care?"

^"I don't think I'm built for that."

^She leans back. Coughs once — a dry, rattling sound. Waves it off before you can ask.
^The screen dims. Before you can process, a shape shimmers into existence beside the pod.
grandpa_revised: ^A shape shimmers into existence beside the pod. Wisps of light where a torso should be, trailing off into nothing.
^Grandpa. But not the Grandpa you remember.
^He floats there, translucent and luminous. An upgraded ghost.
^"Well," he says. "You look like you've been thinking too hard."

^"When I was younger you sounded like a clanker. How'd you get an upgrade?"

c-1: ^"Practice. And better hardware. Death was the start of my finest chapter."

grandpa_philosophy: ^"Life is a lucid dream any way you slice it. It was just yesterday I was watching Matlock, angry at the government. All of a sudden, here we are."

b: ^ "I saw you in there, by the way. The flesh pile." He grins. "Very Greek."
^ "I saw you in there, by the way. Running on that treadmill." He grins. "Very Protestant."

^"Easy for you to say. You're already dead."
^"I don't want to take it lightly. I want it to mean something."

c-1: ^"Dead." He tilts his head. "Is that what this looks like to you?"

^"The meaning was always yours to invent. The machine didn't put you in here. You chose the pleasure dome, or the treadmill, or whatever it was. Same as I chose Matlock."
^"Maybe you just need to experiment more. Be more creative. The canvas is bigger now — that's all."
grandpa_revised_end: ^He starts to fade, edges dissolving into the amber light.
^"Stay or go. It's yours to figure out."
mars_decision: ^Go with your cousin. Choose something difficult.
^Take your grandpa's advice. Enter the dream more boldly.
mars_early_years: ^You'd forgotten how to make decisions. Simple ones. What to eat, when to sleep. Your cousin would ask what you wanted and you'd freeze, waiting for guidance that never came.
^Then, by the third year, you just did things. They worked or they didn't.
sim_reflection: ^You took your grandpa's advice and treated the sim like a place to explore.
^You found yourself learning, creating. Stories. Books. Reflection.
^It led you to realize that while you still had time—before everyone else merged—you should go meet up with your cousin.
^This infinite dream could wait. But those stubborn, free range humans wouldn't upload.
^With a few working years left, you made feeble contributions to her terraforming projects. You simmed some time as a space settler in preparation, and you got pretty good.
^Enough that you felt you'd earned a seat at the table.
interstitial_to_old_age: ^He flips through your file. Pages and pages now.

b: ^"You left early. Traded comfort for agency."
^"You stayed in the system longer than most. Optimized, managed, guided. Then you found your way out."
^"You've made peace with continuation. The long view."
^"You've made peace with endings. That's harder than it sounds."

interstitial_to_old_age: ^"The final stretch now. Let's see what you decide."
old_age_start: ^A retirement community on the Martian plains. The holdouts: humans, dolphins, apes, androids. Anyone who didn't merge.

c-0: ^You don't say it out loud. But you think it.

c-2: ^Biology isn't rudeness. You learned that a long time ago.
c-3: ^You've seen this before. Different bodies, same pattern.

^"Yeah."

^"Turn me into a tomato. That's my upload."

^"We've got to stop meeting like this."
^"Well, I haven't killed it. She'd like that."

b: ^ "You let me in once," it says. "I never forgot that."

tip_banter: ^"Earth merged," it says. "Twenty billion minds. One substrate. No more sim. Just... infinity."
^You look up at the shape in the sky. Your childhood pinwheel. Your tutor.

^"That's horrifying."
^"I almost did that, didn't I?"

c-2: ^"You came close. But here you are."

the_choice: ^The pinwheel's in the sky. Your cousin's in the dirt. Where do you want to go?

s: ^Shed the human. Live forever in the mind of god.
^Die with grace as one of the last free-range humans.
